title: checked if null before freed all variables, but still get memory error
body_html:

(then variable Command stores "setdb", fileName stores "data.txt", Grock- promps again, waiting for user input)

Now if user input is "setdb new.txt" then variable Command stores "setdb", fileName stores "new.txt" below is my code, I freed input, command and fileName, and before I freed them, I checked if they are NULL,

events.body_html: the free() function properly handles being passed a pointer that contains NULL, so no need to check

OT: for ease of readability and understanding: Please consistently indent the code.  Indent after every opening brace '{'.  Unindent before every closing brace '}'.  Suggest each indent level be 4 spaces.

Compile with -Wall; there are a bunch of errors that the compiler will catch. Fix those first, there is a good chance it will solve the problem you're asking about, but even if not should be easier to find the problem.

OT: regarding lines like: if (Command){printf("free command\n");free(Command); Command = NULL;} Please follow the axiom: only one statement per line and (at most) one variable declaration per statement.
OT: when calling fgets() always check (!=NULL) the returned value to assure the operation was successful

this statement: inputStr = getInput(inputStr); is using an uninitialized parameter: inputStr. this statement: Command = getCommand(Command, inputStr); is using an uninitialized parameter: Command. When compiling, always enable the warnings, then fix those warnings ( for gcc, at a minimum use: -Wall -Wextra -Wconversion -pedantic -std=gnu11 ) Note: other compilers use different options to produce the same warnings.

regarding: ainputStr = malloc( (i+1)*sizeof(char) ); 1) this will not work to update the value in function: main() as the address of the variable in main() was not passed. 2) in C, the expression: sizeof(char) is defined as 1, Multiplying anything by 1 has no effect. Suggest removing that expression. 3) Suggest removing the ainputStr parameter. 4) when calling malloc(), always check (!=NULL) the returned value to assure the operation was successful. 5) Suggest: char * ainputStr = malloc( i+1); if( !ainputStr ) { perror( "malloc failed" ); exit( EXIT_FAILURE ); }

regarding: printf("Command malloc fails."); error messages should be output to stderr, When the error indication is from a C library function should also output to stderr the text reason the system thinks the error occurred. The function: perror() exists for that purpose. I.E. perror( "Command malloc fails." );

in function: main(), regarding: fileName = getFileName(fileNameLen, CommandLen, inputLen, inputStr, Command, fileName); Since the returned value may be NULL, the function main() needs to check for this and not proceed as if it does have a file name available.
